requirement_text.REQ-386: Time-limited, expiring signed URLs for instance-attachment byte content, replacing direct unbounded authenticated GET. WHAT EXISTS TODAY: REQ-211/212 built a tenant-isolated attachment store; cross-tenant, cross-instance-same-tenant, malformed/never-issued-UUID, and genuinely-nonexistent-id all fold to the same {:error, :not_found} in fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3, rendered via Response.not_found(conn) -- this behavior is UNCHANGED by REQ-386 and its existing tests (test/letflow/routers/req212_attachments_routes_test.exs, test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs) must still pass untouched. THIS REQUIREMENT added: (1) POST /instances/:id/attachments/:attachment_id/link (:AttachmentsRead-scoped) -- mints a signed, time-limited token (5-minute/300-second expiry) and returns {attachment_id, token, url, expires_at, expires_in_seconds}. (2) GET /instances/:id/attachments/:attachment_id/link-content?link_token=... (:AttachmentsRead-scoped) -- verifies the token before serving content; an expired-or-invalid token returns 410 with a fixed plain-language detail via Response.attachment_link_expired/1, never document bytes. (3) A fresh link request for the same attachment_id after a prior one expired succeeds normally. (4) An expired-or-invalid-token response for a cross-tenant attachment must be byte-identical (status/headers/body) to the response for a token referencing a never-issued attachment id.

result.summary:
Scope test: YES, real executable surface (Letflow.Repository.AttachmentLinks.issue/3+verify/3, two new HTTP routes) -- proceeded to full test-design procedure, not routed to Step 5.

Wrote test/specs/REQ-386.md (16 test cases mapped to all 6 ACs, plus an explicit 'AC4 construction' section walking through the cross-tenant-vs-never-issued mechanism).

Wrote test/letflow/repository/attachment_links_test.exs (12 tests, unit-level, Letflow.DataCase real Postgres): valid round-trip, exact-300s expiry bound, expired via injected clock (both a normal past-expiry case and a strict-boundary case at exactly expires_at), fresh issuance after a prior one expired (AC3's statelessness), malformed token (no separator / bad base64 / bad JSON / empty string, 4 cases), wrong-tenant token (signed under tenant A, verified under tenant B, no expiry involved), tampered payload (payload segment swapped for a different well-formed payload, original signature kept), tampered signature (single byte flipped). Every expiry-dependent case uses AttachmentLinks' own opts[:now] injection -- zero Process.sleep anywhere.

Wrote test/letflow/routers/req386_attachment_links_routes_test.exs (11 tests, route-level, same Letflow.DataCase/dispatch-Instances.call/2 idiom as req212_attachments_routes_test.exs): AC1 (issue response shape, issued link usable before expiry with correct bytes/content-type/content-disposition, 404 for a nonexistent attachment_id on issue), AC2 (expired token -> 410 with the exact fixed detail string and an explicit assertion that neither the real document bytes nor a "content" key appear anywhere in the body; malformed link_token and missing link_token both also -> 410), AC3 (expired attempt fails, then a fresh link for the SAME attachment_id issued via a real POST and used successfully), AC4 (two cases: (a) tenant 2's caller presents tenant 1's validly-issued-but-foreign token against tenant 2's own real, different attachment_id vs. against a fabricated never-issued UUID -- asserted status/content-type header/full resp_body byte-identical, no trace_id normalization needed since build_conn/4 assigns a fixed trace_id on every request, mirroring req212's own established technique; (b) a simpler expired-vs-garbage-token byte-identical case for the same tenant), permission enforcement (AGENT_RUNNER, which this router's own moduledoc documents as holding neither AttachmentsRead nor AttachmentsManage, gets 403 on both new routes).

Since the route handlers (handle_issue_attachment_link/3, handle_get_attachment_link_content/3) call AttachmentLinks.issue/verify with NO now: option of their own (confirmed by reading lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex directly -- the injectable clock is a Letflow.Repository.AttachmentLinks-boundary-only affordance, not threaded through the HTTP layer), every route-level 'expired' test mints an already-past-expiry token directly via AttachmentLinks.issue/3's own now: option (an already-past DateTime.utc_now()-301s) and then presents that token through a normal HTTP GET -- the route's own verify call always uses real wall-clock time, and since the token's own embedded expires_at is already in the past relative to ANY real 'now', it is deterministically expired the instant it's presented. No Process.sleep anywhere in either test file -- confirmed by grep, zero hits.
